_comment: Source for the console's 'How to verify' panels and for PREFLIGHT.md (generated by tools/gen_preflight_doc.py). Steps marked confirm:true haven't been checked against a real tenant yet.

checks.label: Keychain available
checks.what: Writes, reads back and deletes a test entry in the OS keychain (service 'aiguard-se-kit').
checks.why: Every key the kit uses (OneAPI secret, detection and proxy keys) lives only in the keychain. Without it the kit can't save or use keys.
verify: Mac: open Keychain Access, select the login keychain and make sure it shows as unlocked (no padlock).
Mac, after setup: run `security find-generic-password -s aiguard-se-kit -a oneapi-client-secret`. Attributes printed (no secret) means the entry exists.
Windows: Control Panel → Credential Manager → Windows Credentials. Look for entries containing 'aiguard-se-kit'.
Linux: a Secret Service provider must be running (`gnome-keyring-daemon` or KWallet).
fix: Mac: unlock the login keychain (Keychain Access → File → Unlock Keychain "login"). If macOS asks whether Python may access the keychain, choose Always Allow.
Windows: keys go to Credential Manager for the signed-in user. Run the kit as yourself, not from an admin or shared account, and don't use "Run as administrator".
Linux: install and start gnome-keyring, or run the kit from a desktop session.
Managed laptops: if policy blocks keychain access for command-line apps, ask IT for an exception for uv's Python.

checks.label: Detection API reachable
checks.what: Opens an HTTPS connection to the AI Guard Detection API (https://api.us1.zseclipse.net). Any HTTP answer counts as reachable.
checks.why: Every detection-mode test, the guided demo, the live prompt and verification go through this API.
verify: Run `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.us1.zseclipse.net/`.
A number (for example 401, 404 or 405) means the network path is fine.
'SSL certificate problem' or 'unable to get local issuer certificate' means TLS inspection: the Zscaler root CA isn't trusted by the tool.
'Could not resolve host' means DNS or a proxy setting; 'Connection timed out' means a firewall or proxy is blocking it.
fix: Start the kit with ./aiguard-kit (it trusts the OS certificate store) and make sure the Zscaler root CA is in the System keychain (Mac) or Trusted Root store (Windows).
If your tenant is on another AI Guard cloud, set AIGUARD_DAS_HOST before running, e.g. `AIGUARD_DAS_HOST=https://api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net ./aiguard-kit preflight`.
On a restricted network, ask for api.*.zseclipse.net to be allowed.
checks.confirm_note: us1 is the only Detection API host confirmed so far; other cloud host names are unverified.

checks.label: AI Guard proxy reachable
checks.what: Opens an HTTPS connection to the AI Guard proxy (https://proxy.zseclipse.net).
checks.why: Only needed for LLM proxy mode (real model calls and token usage). Detection mode works without it, so this is a warning, not a failure.
verify: Run `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://proxy.zseclipse.net/`. A number means reachable; read errors as for the Detection API check.
fix: Same as the Detection API check. To use another proxy host, set AIGUARD_PROXY.

checks.label: OneAPI credentials saved
checks.what: Confirms a vanity domain and client ID are saved in ~/.aiguard-se-kit/config.json and the client secret is in the keychain.
checks.why: Every configuration call to your tenant uses these.
verify: Open ~/.aiguard-se-kit/config.json: it should show vanity_domain and client_id (never the secret).
The vanity domain is only the subdomain: 'acme' for acme.zslogin.net.
fix: Console: Setup → step 1 → Use different credentials. Terminal: rerun `./aiguard-kit setup` and decline the saved credentials.

checks.label: OneAPI login
checks.what: Gets an OAuth token from ZIdentity with the client ID and secret, then lists AI Guard policies.
checks.why: Proves the credentials, vanity domain and API scope work together.
verify: ZIdentity admin portal → Integration → API Clients: the client exists, is enabled, and its secret hasn't been rotated since you saved it.
The client's resources/scopes include AI Guard.
The error text tells you which part failed: 'invalid_client' = ID or secret; a name-resolution error = vanity domain; 401 = scope.
fix: invalid_client: copy the client ID again and create a new secret, then re-enter both in step 1.
Name resolution: re-enter the vanity domain as the bare subdomain.
401 / not authorized: add AI Guard to the API client's scopes in ZIdentity and save.
checks.confirm_note: The exact label of the AI Guard scope in ZIdentity hasn't been captured yet; update this text from a screenshot.

checks.label: Read access to AI Guard
checks.what: Lists policies, rules, providers, provider credentials, apps and app credentials.
checks.why: Setup needs the current state to avoid duplicates and pick rule order.
verify: The detail line shows counts. Compare them with the AI Security console: AI Guard policies, rules and AI Applications.
fix: A failure on one list (for example 'Read llm provider credentials') means the API client's AI Guard access is partial. Give it full AI Guard access.
checks.retest: `./aiguard-kit preflight` → ✓ Read access to AI Guard

checks.label: Create and delete permission
checks.what: Optional probe: creates an app named '<prefix>: preflight probe' and deletes it immediately.
checks.why: Without create permission, setup fails at its first object. Finding out here means nothing is half-created.
verify: AI Security console → AI Applications: there should be no '<prefix>: preflight probe' app afterwards.
In ZIdentity, the API client's AI Guard access should be full, not read-only.
fix: Grant the API client full AI Guard access, save, wait a minute, then run the checks again.
If a probe app was left behind (only possible if the delete failed), delete it in the console or run teardown.
checks.confirm_note: The ZIdentity wording for read-only vs full AI Guard access hasn't been confirmed.

checks.label: OpenAI provider available
checks.what: Looks for an LLM provider of type 'openai' in the tenant.
checks.why: Only needed for proxy mode with OpenAI. Detection mode is unaffected.
verify: AI Security console → LLM providers: a provider of type OpenAI is listed (tenants normally include 'Default OpenAI Provider').
fix: If it's missing, add an OpenAI provider in the console, or skip proxy mode for this app.
checks.confirm_note: Console menu name for providers not captured yet.

checks.label: Anthropic provider available
checks.what: Looks for an LLM provider of type 'anthropic' in the tenant.
checks.why: Only needed for proxy mode with Anthropic. Detection mode is unaffected.
verify: AI Security console → LLM providers: a provider of type Anthropic is listed (normally 'Default Anthropic Provider').
fix: If it's missing, add an Anthropic provider in the console, or skip proxy mode for this app.
checks.confirm_note: Console menu name for providers not captured yet.

checks.label: Earlier kit objects
checks.what: Counts policies, rules and apps whose names start with the kit prefix (default 'SE-Demo:').
checks.why: Lets setup keep and fill in an earlier setup, or replace it, instead of creating duplicates.
verify: Search the console for 'SE-Demo:' in policies, rules and AI Applications.
fix: Nothing to fix. In step 3, choose Keep (fill in gaps) or Delete and start fresh.
If someone else in a shared tenant uses the same prefix, run the kit with --prefix 'SE-Demo-<yourname>'.

checks.label: No broad rules ahead of the kit's
checks.what: Looks for enabled rules that don't match by application (for example match type USER).
checks.why: The kit's rules match only its own apps, so app-based rules can't take its traffic. A rule that matches by user might, and then that rule's policy judges the demo traffic.
verify: AI Guard policy rules in the console: check the listed rules' match criteria and order.
After setup, verification reports which policy actually handled each app's test scan. If it names the kit's policy, the warning didn't matter.
fix: If verification shows another policy: disable that rule for the demo, narrow its users, or move the kit's rules above it in the console.
Then press Retry checks (console) or run `./aiguard-kit status`.
checks.retest: Verification after setup → ✓ '<app>: Detection API … policy '<prefix>: Test all''
checks.confirm_note: Whether user-matched rules apply to Detection API scans that carry a user hasn't been tested.

checks.label: Reused policy covers the tests
checks.what: Only when you reuse an existing policy: compares its enabled detectors with the kit's template.
checks.why: Each missing detector leaves a console panel empty (for example no prompt_tags = no Prompt Classifications).
verify: Open the policy in the console and check the listed detectors are enabled for prompts and responses.
fix: Enable the missing detectors in the console, or let setup create the kit's own policy (recommended; it can also be switched between Monitor and Enforce).
checks.retest: `./aiguard-kit preflight` → ✓ Reused policy covers the tests

checks.label: Tenant Settings > Security > Store Prompts/Responses
checks.what: A reminder. This setting can't be read through the API.
checks.why: When it's off, events still appear but prompt and response text isn't shown in event details.
verify: AI Security console → Tenant Settings → Security → Store Prompts/Responses is on.
fix: Turn it on and save. It applies to new events only.
checks.retest: Run one test, then open its event in the console and check the prompt text shows.

checks.label: Verification: handled by the demo policy
checks.what: After setup, scans one prompt through each app's detection key and compares the policy that handled it with the kit's policy. Retries for about a minute while new keys activate.
checks.why: This is the end-to-end proof that keys, rules and policy are wired correctly.
verify: ✓ lines name the kit's policy and show a response time.
In the console, AI Guard events for the apps '<prefix>: OpenAI App' and '<prefix>: Anthropic App' appear within a few minutes.
fix: 'handled by … instead': another rule matched first (see 'No broad rules ahead of the kit's').
401 / 404 after a minute: the key isn't active or was deleted. Rerun setup (it recreates missing keys).
400 mentioning authenticate-llm-app: the request used a proxy key. Rerun setup to create detection keys.
checks.retest: Console: Retry checks on the last setup step. Terminal: `./aiguard-kit status`.
